entries.title: Delete a live-captured session's transcript and recording
entries.summary: Sessions captured with Live Transcribe can now be deleted: **Delete** on the **Live session** card in **Media → Library**, **Actions → Delete live session** on the session's page, or **Delete** on a row of **Transcribe → Captured sessions**. It permanently removes the transcript, saved audio, AI summary, insights, translations, highlights, comments and podcast; the session itself stays on the agenda.

where.path: Marketing → Media → Library → Live session card ⋯ → Delete; live session page → Actions → Delete live session; Marketing → Transcribe → Captured sessions → Delete

entries.use_case: Teams that ran test captures before the event, or captured a session that should never have been recorded, can now remove it themselves so it disappears from Media, Captured sessions and the attendee view — without touching the session on the agenda.

cs_action.note: Deleting a live capture is permanent: there is no Trash and no Restore, unlike uploaded recordings. Make sure the customer means it before they click.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer asks how to remove test captures or a session captured by mistake, or asks why a live session card had no Delete.
internal.who_should_get_it: Any customer using Live Transcribe, especially ahead of a show where test captures were run.
internal.staff_path: Marketing → Media → Library → Live session card ⋯ → Delete
internal.gotchas: Hard delete — the live-capture tables have no archive, so nothing comes back. Uploaded Recording cards keep Trash + Restore. Needs an active org member or an event user of that event; others get Forbidden. The deletion is written to the audit trail as session.transcript.deleted.
internal.talk_track: You can now delete a live capture yourself from the Media library, the session page or Captured sessions. It is permanent, and your agenda is untouched.

entries.title: Combined character limits now hold on every edit, with a live counter in the speaker portal
entries.summary: A submission form's **Cross-field character limits** now apply after submission too: edits from the speaker portal's session panel, the Sessions grid and drawer, follow-up forms and the public API are checked against the combined total and refused with the rule's message when they would go over. Edits that shorten an over-limit abstract are always accepted. In the portal, **Edit** on a session shows a counter per rule under **Save**, which stays disabled while the text is over the limit.

where.path: Speaker portal → My sessions → session → Edit; Sessions grid and drawer; public API

entries.use_case: Programs with a combined word budget for an abstract — common for medical and scientific calls — can rely on it: speakers and staff can no longer push a submission past the limit after it was accepted, and speakers see the count while they edit instead of being surprised later.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer finds abstracts over their combined character limit, or asks whether the limit still applies once speakers edit in the portal.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers with cross-field character rules on a submission form, especially abstract calls for medical and scientific meetings.
internal.staff_path: Program → Forms → [form] → Form Settings → Cross-field character limits
internal.gotchas: Abstracts already over the limit are not truncated; they stay as they are and can only be trimmed (any edit that grows the total is refused). Rules are per form: a session that came in through a second form without the rule is not limited. Only session-scope rules are enforced on these edit paths; translated (locale) variants are not counted.
internal.talk_track: Your combined character limit now holds everywhere the abstract can be edited, and speakers see a live count in their portal while they edit.

entries.title: Portal hides the session room when Location is hidden
entries.summary: When **Location** is not among a portal's visible **Submission Fields** (**Manage Fields → Show/Hide Fields**), the session's room no longer shows anywhere in the portal: the home page session list, the calendar, task headers or the session panel. Portals where no visible fields were ever chosen still show every field, including the room.

where.path: Portals → [portal] → Manage Fields → Submission Fields → Show/Hide Fields

entries.use_case: Organizers who keep room assignments private until the program is final can now rely on hiding Location in the portal: speakers no longer see a room the team has not published.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer says speakers can see rooms in the portal even though Location is hidden.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers who hide Location (room) from speakers or sponsors in their portal configuration.
internal.staff_path: Portals → [portal] → Manage Fields → Submission Fields → Show/Hide Fields
internal.gotchas: Only portals with an explicit visible-fields list are affected. A portal that never had Show/Hide Fields saved shows every field, room included — to hide the room there, save a visible list without Location.
internal.talk_track: Hide Location in the portal's fields and the room is hidden everywhere in the portal.

entries.title: Answer option rules on Tags, Track, Format, Level and Language
entries.summary: In the session form builder, **Use question rules** on a **Tags**, **Track**, **Format**, **Level** or **Language** question now shows the **Answer option rules** tab, listing that catalog's answers from Program settings. You can set rules such as *show Tag A when Track is Track 1* from the builder instead of only on custom dropdowns.

where.path: Program → Forms → [form] → question ⋯ → Use question rules → Answer option rules

entries.use_case: Programs that want submitters to see only the tags or formats that fit the track they chose can now set that up themselves in the form builder, which keeps long tag lists manageable.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer wants tags (or formats, levels) to depend on the track a submitter picks, or reports the Answer option rules tab missing on Tags or Track.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers with long tag or format lists that differ by track.
internal.staff_path: Program → Forms → [form] → Tags question ⋯ → Use question rules
internal.gotchas: Rules are matched on the answer's text without regard to case, so a rule on "Tag A" also applies to a tag named "tag a" (SB-10458, not fixed yet). If a catalog is empty, the tab stays hidden.
internal.talk_track: You can now make tags, formats, levels and languages depend on earlier answers right in the form builder.

entries.title: Self check-in kiosks
entries.summary: Turn an iPad or Android tablet running the Attend app into a self check-in kiosk locked to one event, set up under **Onsite → Check-in & badges → Self check-in kiosks**. Attendees find their registration by wallet or app badge, an emailed 6-digit code, or last name plus confirmation number, check in and print their badge. You choose the printer, the reprint policy and the staff PIN per kiosk.

where.path: Onsite → Check-in & badges → Self check-in kiosks

entries.use_case: Events with a queue at registration can let most attendees check themselves in and print their own badge, keeping the staff desk free for walk-ups and questions.

cs_action.note: Registration is Early Access; the event needs Registration enabled before kiosks appear.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a Registration customer plans onsite check-in with badge printing and expects queues.
internal.who_should_get_it: Registration Early Access customers running onsite check-in with badge printers.
internal.staff_path: Onsite → Check-in & badges → Self check-in kiosks
internal.gotchas: The QR code in the confirmation email works only at the staff desk, not at a kiosk — kiosks need the wallet pass or app badge, the emailed code, or last name plus confirmation number. Kiosks never search by name or list registrants. Check the supported printers list in the article.
internal.talk_track: Put a few tablets at the door and most attendees check themselves in and print their badge; your staff handle the exceptions.

entries.title: Slack: ask Sessionboard about your events and get notifications in Slack
entries.summary: The **Slack** app is in **Apps** for every organization. Connect your workspace once, and each person can turn on the **Slack** column in their notification preferences to get Sessionboard notifications as Slack messages. Organizations hosted in the United States with AI features on can also ask about their event data in the app's chat, with `/sessionboard`, or by @mentioning it in a channel — answers run under each person's own Sessionboard permissions.

enable.path: Apps → Slack → Set up Slack → Connect with Slack

where.path: Apps → Slack; in Slack: the Sessionboard app, /sessionboard, @Sessionboard; notification preferences → Slack column

entries.use_case: Your team gets answers about speakers, sessions and submissions where they already work, without opening Sessionboard, and notifications land in Slack with a link back to the record.

cs_action.note: Self-serve from Apps. Needs AI features on for the org; askers need a Sessionboard account with the same email as their Slack account.

internal.when_to_bring_up: Any team that lives in Slack and asks 'how many speakers have confirmed?' type questions, or wants notifications outside email.
internal.who_should_get_it: US-hosted organizations with AI features on. EU and Middle East organizations can connect and receive Slack notifications, but questions asked in Slack are answered for US-hosted organizations only.
internal.staff_path: Apps → Slack (staff see the same page). Usage and installs post to #engineering-logs-team-lead once the activity log ships.
internal.gotchas: @mention answers are visible to the whole channel; /sessionboard and the app's chat are private. /sessionboard doesn't work inside threads. Slack guests and people from other organizations in shared channels are refused. One Slack workspace per Sessionboard organization.
internal.talk_track: Connect Slack once and your whole team can ask Sessionboard questions right in Slack — each person only sees what they can see in Sessionboard.

entries.title: Find my events: sign in to every event with one code in the Attend app
entries.summary: Attendees and speakers who don't have their event code can tap **Find my events** in the Attend mobile app, enter their email address or phone number, and receive a single 6-digit code. After entering the code they see every event they are registered for — across all regions — and can open any of them with one tap, without a second sign-in step. Organizers' **My Profile** page now also accepts a phone number, which is used to match the person across events via SMS.

where.path: Attend mobile app → sign-in screen → Find my events

entries.use_case: Attendees and speakers who arrive at an event without their event code or invitation email can identify themselves with just an email or phone number and get straight into the app — no organizer intervention needed.

cs_action.note: The feature is server-side only in this PR; the mobile app UI ships separately. Confirm the Attend app client release is live before telling customers. Also confirm Doppler env vars (ATTEND_IDENTITY_PEERS, ATTEND_IDENTITY_SERVICE_PRIVATE_KEY/PUBLIC_KEY) are set in prod-us, prod-eu and prod-me — without them each region answers for itself only and cross-region event lists won't appear.

internal.when_to_bring_up: Any event using the Attend app where attendees or speakers frequently contact support because they can't find their event code or sign-in link.
internal.who_should_get_it: All Attend Mobile App customers, especially large conferences with attendees across multiple events or regions.
internal.gotchas: Speakers with no attendee registration row get a null grant with reason 'no_registration' — they will see the event listed but cannot tap into it until they have a registration. Events requiring SSO show 'sso_required' and also cannot be opened via this flow. Phone numbers are deduplicated by most-recent login; a shared number goes to the account that signed in most recently.
internal.talk_track: Attendees no longer need to hunt for their event code. They type their email or phone, get one code, and see every event they're part of — all in a few seconds.

draft.docs_gap: The /attend/mobile-app guide should add a section explaining the Find my events sign-in flow from the attendee perspective, including what happens when a grant is unavailable (no registration or SSO required).
draft.why_use_it: The Attend mobile app puts the full event experience — agenda, networking, session check-in, Q&A and more — in attendees' and speakers' hands. Find my events removes the last barrier to getting in: anyone who is already registered or assigned to a session can reach every event they belong to by verifying their identity once, even across multiple events or regions.

entries.title: Onsite check-in, badge formats, and Advocacy join page get security-hardened UI
entries.summary: Several onsite and marketing surfaces now enforce tighter security defaults. **Badge Formats**: a format that the system has switched off now shows **"Turned off"** instead of appearing selectable. **Print Station**: the claim-attempt token is passed back on the PDF URL and the done screen only when the server returns it, preventing stale claim data. **Advocacy join page**: the post-join screen now instructs members to confirm from the email they received; an expired-verification link shows a clear **"?verify=expired"** notice (available in English, German, French, and Spanish). **Companion / company links**: posting directly to LinkedIn is disabled on company links; clips share through LinkedIn's native share dialog instead.

where.path: Registration → Onsite → Badge Formats; Registration → Onsite → Print Station; Marketing → Advocacy (join page); Marketing → Create → Companion / company links

entries.use_case: Organizers running onsite check-in get clearer feedback when a badge format is unavailable, and claim data is only surfaced when the server confirms it — reducing the risk of incorrect badge prints. Advocacy members joining through a group link now see actionable guidance when their verification link has expired.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer reports confusion about disabled badge formats or stale claim data at the print station, or when Advocacy members report unclear join-confirmation messaging.
internal.who_should_get_it: Any customer using onsite badge printing or Advocacy group join links.
internal.staff_path: Registration → Onsite → Badge Formats; Marketing → Advocacy
internal.gotchas: These changes are safe to deploy before the companion API PR (web-api #4887) ships — all new response fields are optional and nothing new is sent to an API that did not return it. The LinkedIn direct-post change on company links may surprise customers who expected that path to work.
internal.talk_track: The print station and badge format UI now stay in sync with what the server actually supports, so your desk staff see 'Turned off' instead of a broken format, and claim tokens only appear when the server confirms them.

draft.docs_gap: The onsite check-in guide should add a note explaining the "Turned off" badge format state and how claim-attempt tokens appear on the print station done screen.
draft.why_use_it: Sessionboard's onsite check-in and badge printing tools let event teams process arrivals quickly and accurately at the desk. Badge format controls, print-station claim tracking, and Advocacy join flows are designed to surface only what the server has confirmed, so staff and attendees always act on accurate information.

entries.title: Account phone hint clarified to state the one-account rule only
entries.summary: The hint text beneath the **Phone** field in **Account Settings** now reads "Include the country code. A number can be on only one account." The previous wording implied the phone number could be used to find events; that is no longer the case. Updated in English, German, Spanish, and French.

where.path: Account Settings → Phone

entries.use_case: Users who read the old hint and expected their phone number to help them locate events will no longer be misled; the hint now accurately describes what the field does.

internal.when_to_bring_up: Only if a customer reports confusion about phone-number behaviour after the related API change (web-api#4888).
internal.who_should_get_it: All users — the hint is visible to anyone who opens Account Settings.
internal.staff_path: Account Settings → Phone
internal.gotchas: A companion API change (web-api#4888) removed the ability for an unconfirmed account phone to find Attend events; this copy fix aligns the UI with that behaviour.

draft.docs_gap: The account-settings phone field and its one-account constraint are not documented in any current guide; a short note in the 2FA or account-settings article would help users understand why a number can only appear on one account.
draft.why_use_it: null

entries.title: Speaker Prospects agenda crawls are more accurate and now capture job title, company, photo and profile links
entries.summary: The **Recon** crawler that pulls sessions and speakers from external agenda pages now learns each agenda's layout once and replays that knowledge on every subsequent crawl — no AI on repeat runs. Speakers discovered on the page now include job title, company, photo and profile links when the page shows them. Paginated agendas are followed page by page; a crawl that cannot load every page is marked **partial** and never removes existing sessions. Failed crawls explain why they failed.

where.path: Speaker CRM → Prospects → External Events → Agenda tab → Run now

entries.use_case: Teams prospecting speakers from competitor or partner events get richer, more reliable data — including speaker bios, photos and company — without manual copy-paste, and without losing previously found sessions if a crawl hits a pagination limit.

cs_action.note: The crawl engine is fully replaced. Recipes are stored per external event; the first crawl after deploy triggers an AI investigation run (Anthropic API key and RECON_* env vars must be set in Doppler, plus 2 DB migrations). Crawls that cannot generate a valid recipe fail gracefully and keep existing data.

internal.when_to_bring_up: Any customer using Speaker Prospects / Recon who has complained about missed sessions, stale speaker data, or crawl failures on JavaScript-heavy agenda pages.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers on the speaker_prospects beta who actively monitor external events for speaker sourcing.
internal.staff_path: Speaker CRM → Prospects → External Events
internal.gotchas: First crawl per external event now costs up to ~US$4 in Anthropic API calls to generate the recipe. If the agenda tool (Sched, Bizzabo, Swoogo, etc.) changes its layout, a new investigation run is triggered. A daily spend cap and back-off are in place. Paginated agendas that exceed the page cap are marked 'partial' — sessions are never removed on a partial crawl.
internal.talk_track: Recon now learns each agenda site's structure once and replays it instantly on every future crawl — so your prospect list stays current, speakers come in with their full profile details, and you never lose data from a partial crawl.

draft.docs_gap: The Speaker Prospects guide should document the recipe-based crawl lifecycle (investigate → verify → replay), the 'partial' crawl status, the richer speaker fields now captured, and what a crawl failure message looks like.
draft.why_use_it: Speaker Prospects lets you monitor external event agendas and automatically pull in sessions and speakers as potential candidates for your own program. It keeps your prospect pipeline fresh without manual research, surfaces speaker details like job title, company and headshot directly from the source page, and flags crawl issues so you always know the state of your data.

entries.title: Account Settings now validates phone numbers and prevents duplicates across accounts
entries.summary: The **Phone** field in **Account Settings** now shows inline validation errors: "This number is already on another account." when a number is taken, and "That doesn't look like a phone number." when the format is invalid. A hint under the field reminds users to include the country code, explains that each number can belong to only one account, and notes that the phone number is used to find your events in the Attend app. A bug is also fixed where a taken phone number would incorrectly report the email address as already in use.

where.path: Account Settings → Phone

entries.use_case: Any user who enters a phone number in their account settings gets immediate, specific feedback if the number is already taken or formatted incorrectly, preventing silent failures and confusion — especially important for speakers and attendees who rely on their phone number to find their events in the Attend app.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a speaker or attendee reports they cannot find their events in the Attend app, or when a user is confused by an error message on Account Settings.
internal.who_should_get_it: All users; no action needed — this is on by default once the paired API change (web-api#4888) is deployed.
internal.gotchas: The new error codes (phone_taken, phone_invalid) only appear once the API PR lennd/sessionboard-web-api#4888 is live; before that, the UI behaves as before. Also fixes a pre-existing bug where a taken phone number would incorrectly surface as an email conflict.
internal.talk_track: If a speaker says they can't find their events in Attend, check that their phone number is saved correctly in Account Settings — the field now tells them immediately if the number is already on another account or formatted wrong.

draft.docs_gap: The Account Settings page (phone number field, Attend app lookup behaviour, and one-account-per-number rule) is not covered by any existing guide; the closest article is the 2FA settings page. A short section or standalone guide on managing account profile settings — including phone number requirements for the Attend app — should be added.
draft.why_use_it: Your phone number is how the Attend app locates your events — keeping it accurate and unique to your account ensures you always find the right events when you sign in. Clear inline errors mean you know exactly what to fix without guessing.

entries.title: Install the Slack app from Slack, and removing it there disconnects Sessionboard
entries.summary: Clicking **Add to Slack** from Slack now finishes in Sessionboard: after you allow the app, Sessionboard asks which organization to connect the workspace to, and you're done. Removing the app from your Slack workspace now disconnects it in Sessionboard automatically.

enable.path: Apps → Slack → Connect (or install from the Slack App Directory, then complete on the Apps → Slack → Connect page)

where.path: Apps → Slack

entries.use_case: Teams who discover the Sessionboard Slack app in the Slack Marketplace can install it without switching to Sessionboard first. When a workspace admin removes the app from Slack, the connection is cleaned up automatically so stale or revoked tokens never linger.

cs_action.note: No manual steps required. The Slack app settings for the production app (A0BDH69PSMC) must have the Direct Install URL set and bot events subscribed — this is a post-deploy ops task, not a customer action.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer asks how to install the Sessionboard Slack app from the Slack App Directory, or when they report a stale Slack connection after uninstalling the app from their workspace.
internal.who_should_get_it: Any organization using the Slack integration, especially those who manage app installs centrally through the Slack Admin console.
internal.staff_path: Apps → Slack
internal.gotchas: A workspace connects to one organization: installing into a workspace already connected elsewhere is refused with "already connected to another Sessionboard organization". An install link expires after 30 minutes.
internal.talk_track: Your team can now find and install the Sessionboard Slack app straight from the Slack App Directory. If a workspace admin ever removes it, the connection clears itself automatically — no orphaned tokens.

draft.docs_gap: The App Marketplace guide has no section covering the Slack direct-install flow or the automatic revocation behaviour on uninstall; a dedicated Slack integration guide (similar to the Zoom or Docusign guides) should document both paths.
draft.why_use_it: Connecting Sessionboard to Slack lets your team receive notifications and updates in the channels where they already work. The direct-install flow means anyone who finds the app in the Slack Marketplace can authorize it immediately and then pick the right Sessionboard organization — no need to start from inside Sessionboard. Automatic revocation keeps your connected apps list accurate when a workspace admin removes the integration from the Slack side.

entries.title: Registration privacy: consent management, DSAR export, anonymisation and retention
entries.summary: A new **Privacy** panel under **Registration › Settings › Privacy** lets organizers choose between **Basic** and **Full GDPR** privacy modes. **Full GDPR** mode adds Data Protection Officer fields, a versioned data-processing consent text, and a configurable retention rule that anonymises registrants N months after the event ends. Both modes support adding, editing and removing consent questions (each versioned automatically when wording changes). **Full GDPR** mode also unlocks privacy tools — **Consent log**, **History**, per-person **Export data** and **Anonymise**, and a retention **Preview / Run now** workflow — all gated behind the new **Export and anonymise registrant data** permission. In the registrant drawer, a **Consent** section lists each consent with its version and answer; an **Anonymised** banner appears on anonymised records. On the registrants list, **More → Anonymise…** lets admins bulk-anonymise selected registrations after a dry-run preview and a typed confirmation.

where.path: Registration › Settings › Privacy; Registration › Registrants (drawer Consent section and Anonymised banner; More → Anonymise…)

entries.use_case: Events operating under GDPR or similar privacy regulations can capture versioned consent at registration, respond to data subject access requests with a one-click JSON export, and automatically anonymise registrant records on a configurable schedule — all without leaving Sessionboard.

cs_action.note: This UI depends on web-api lennd/sessionboard-web-api#4884. Until that API is live the Privacy panel reads defaults and shows a 'needs the latest API' message. Confirm the API PR is merged and deployed before pointing any customer at this feature.

internal.when_to_bring_up: Any customer who mentions GDPR compliance, consent capture, data subject access requests, or a need to purge registrant PII after an event.
internal.who_should_get_it: Events with European attendees or any org with a formal data-retention policy; particularly associations, medical societies and enterprise customers.
internal.staff_path: Registration › Settings › Privacy
internal.gotchas: The 'Export and anonymise registrant data' permission is new and not yet in the standard permission slugs list — confirm the exact slug with engineering before documenting it. Anonymisation is irreversible; the dry-run step and typed confirmation (ANONYMISE) are the only safeguards. Order totals are preserved after anonymisation.
internal.talk_track: You can now collect versioned consent on your registration form, export a registrant's full data record in one click for a DSAR, and set a retention rule that automatically anonymises records after the event — all audited and logged inside Sessionboard.

draft.docs_gap: The linked guide /registration/privacy appears to already exist in the article index and covers this feature; confirm the guide is published and includes the exact permission name for 'Export and anonymise registrant data' and the typed-confirmation word (ANONYMISE vs ANONYMIZE) that the UI requires.
draft.why_use_it: Registration privacy gives you a structured way to collect, version and audit registrant consent, respond to data subject access requests, and remove personal data on a schedule that matches your retention policy. Use Basic mode for lightweight consent questions, or switch to Full GDPR mode to add a Data Protection Officer, a versioned processing statement, per-person export and anonymisation tools, and an automated retention run. Every consent answer is logged with its version, timestamp and source IP so you have a complete audit trail if a regulator asks.

entries.title: Registration privacy: consent management, DSAR export, anonymisation and retention
entries.summary: A new **Settings › Privacy** section for Registration events lets organizers choose a privacy mode, collect and version custom consent questions, and view an append-only **Consent Log**. In **Full GDPR** mode, a required data-processing consent checkbox and DPO contact appear on the public form and in registration emails. Registrants can withdraw individual consents from their manage link or the attendee portal. A new **privacy_manage** permission gates three additional tools: **Export** (one JSON document of everything the event holds on a person), **Anonymise** (irreversibly removes PII while keeping financial and tax records intact, with a dry-run option), and **Retention** (schedules automatic anonymisation N months after the event ends). Existing GDPR-request and Pathways person-delete paths now anonymise Registration rows instead of deleting them.

enable.path: Get started → Early Access → Preview → Registration; then Settings › Privacy

where.path: Settings › Privacy

entries.use_case: Events that must comply with GDPR or similar privacy regulations can capture explicit, versioned consent at checkout, give registrants a self-serve withdrawal path, and respond to data-subject access requests with a single export — all without leaving Sessionboard. Retention automation removes PII on a schedule so organizers do not have to remember to act after the event closes.

cs_action.note: Feature is behind the Registration Early Access gate. Full GDPR mode changes the public checkout form (adds a required consent checkbox and DPO line) and registration emails (adds {{dpo_line}} merge tag). Review with customers before enabling Full GDPR mode on a live event. The new privacy_manage permission is seeded to every role that already holds settings_manage, so day-one reach is unchanged — but customers may want to restrict it to their DPO only.

internal.when_to_bring_up: Any Registration customer who has asked about GDPR compliance, data-subject requests, or post-event data deletion.
internal.who_should_get_it: Events subject to GDPR or similar privacy laws, especially those in the EU/UK or handling medical/professional data; any org with a dedicated DPO.
internal.staff_path: Event → Settings › Privacy
internal.gotchas: Full GDPR mode adds a required, unticked consent checkbox to the public checkout — enabling it on a live form will immediately affect registrations in progress. Anonymisation is irreversible; the dry-run option should always be demonstrated first. Retention runs daily at 04:17 UTC by default; the first run after the due date anonymises all eligible rows. Spreedly stored-payment redaction happens after the DB commit and is async.
internal.talk_track: If you need to show auditors exactly what each registrant consented to, respond to a GDPR erasure request in minutes, or automatically clean up PII after your event, Registration Privacy handles all three — with a consent log that is append-only and an anonymisation that keeps your financial records intact.

draft.docs_gap: The linked guide /registration/privacy is listed in the article index and appears to be the correct destination; confirm the guide covers the privacy_manage permission, the Full GDPR checkout flow, the {{dpo_line}} email merge tag, and the retention dry-run vs. live-run distinction.
draft.why_use_it: Registration Privacy gives you a complete, auditable record of what each registrant agreed to and when, so you can demonstrate compliance without spreadsheets or manual tracking. Registrants can withdraw specific consents at any time from their manage link, and those withdrawals flow immediately into email, SMS, Pathways and CRM. When a data-subject access or erasure request arrives, a single export or anonymisation covers registrations, orders, answers, consent history and more — with financial and tax records preserved. Retention lets you set a policy once and have anonymisation run automatically after the event ends.

entries.title: Set up registration with Team Lead: attendee types, tickets, forms, payments and emails
entries.summary: **Team Lead** can now walk an organizer through building a registration setup end-to-end. It reads the current state of **Registration** (attendee types, tickets, member pricing, date tiers, forms, payment gateway, sender, confirmation email) and makes changes on the organizer's behalf — creating or updating attendee types, ticket types, registration forms (always saved as **Draft**), the **From** name and address on registration emails, and the confirmation email subject, preview, body and button. Selecting a payment gateway requires the organizer's existing Spreedly gateway nickname and the same merchant-manager permission and recent second-factor check that the **Registration › Settings › Payments** page enforces. Team Lead also answers questions about registration performance — funnel (views → checkouts → completions), waitlist, orders, payments, capacity and member counts — using the same numbers shown on the **Registration Overview**.

enable.path: Get started → Early Access → Preview → Registration; Team Lead is available in the Agent window once Registration Early Access is on.

where.path: Agent window → Team Lead; Registration → Overview, Forms, Tickets, Settings

entries.use_case: Organizers who are setting up registration for the first time — or reconfiguring it before a new event — can describe what they want in plain language and let Team Lead build the draft structure, then review and approve each change before anything goes live.

cs_action.note: Registration Early Access must be on for the event before Team Lead's registration tools appear. The payment-gateway tool reuses the existing merchant-manager permission and second-factor check — SSO-only admins without local 2FA enrollment will get an error and must set the gateway manually in Registration › Settings › Payments (known limitation, follow-up story).

internal.when_to_bring_up: Any customer who has Registration and is configuring a new event, or who asks how to check registration funnel numbers without building a custom report.
internal.who_should_get_it: Events with Registration (beta) enabled; especially customers new to the module or running multiple events who want to replicate a setup quickly.
internal.staff_path: Event sidebar → Agent window → Team Lead
internal.gotchas: Forms created or updated by Team Lead are always saved as Draft; Team Lead cannot publish a form live. Drag individuals onto tables, let the auto-seat engine group people by company or order, and produce print-ready table tents and place cards in one step. entries.title: Registration gets admin notification rules and a full SMS panel

draft.why_use_it: Registration notifications and SMS let you close the loop between a registration event and the people who need to act on it. SMS reaches attendees directly on their phones for time-sensitive onsite messages, opt-in reminders, and last-minute notices — all managed from the same Registration module where you built the event.

entries.title: Void, merge duplicate, and view-as actions in the registrant drawer
entries.summary: Three new actions are available in the registrant drawer. **Void** cancels a registration with an optional reason and shows a banner explaining it is not a refund; if money was collected, a toast directs you to **Orders** to issue the refund. **Merge duplicate** lets you search for the registration to keep, previews exactly what moves (orders, payments, answers, workshop picks, seats, check-in, scans, staff notes, badge history, credits, saved payment methods, member ID), then voids the duplicate and opens the surviving record. **View as registrant** opens the read-only attendee portal in a new tab and logs the action in History. Voided registrations show a banner with the void date, reason, and a link to the record they were merged into, and all other actions are disabled. A **Voided** status filter is also added to the Registrants list.

where.path: Registration → Registrants → open a registrant drawer → Void / Merge duplicate / View as registrant

entries.use_case: Use Void to cancel a registration that should no longer count without deleting its history, and use Merge duplicate to consolidate two records for the same person — moving all orders, payments, answers, and check-in data to one clean record — without charging or refunding anything. Use View as registrant to confirm exactly what the attendee portal shows before a registrant calls in with a question.

cs_action.note: Feature is behind the existing feature--registration gate (Registration beta). Void is not a refund — if an order has a paid balance, the organizer must go to Orders to refund it separately. Merge is irreversible: the duplicate record is voided and the survivor keeps all data. View-as is logged in History.

internal.when_to_bring_up: Any Registration beta customer who has duplicate registrant records or needs to cancel a registration without a full refund.
internal.who_should_get_it: All Registration beta customers automatically — no additional flag needed.
internal.staff_path: Registration → Registrants → open a registrant drawer
internal.gotchas: Void does not issue a refund; CSMs should remind customers to refund from Orders first if money was collected. Merge cannot be undone — the voided duplicate record shows a banner linking to the survivor but cannot be restored.
internal.talk_track: If you end up with two records for the same person, Merge duplicate moves everything — payments, answers, check-in, badges — to the record you want to keep and voids the other one, with nothing charged or refunded. Void lets you cancel a registration and keep the audit trail intact.

draft.docs_gap: The /registration/registrants guide should add a "Void or merge a duplicate" section and a "View as a registrant" section covering the new drawer actions, the voided-registration banner, and the Voided status filter.
draft.why_use_it: The Registrants drawer gives organizers a single place to act on individual registrations without leaving the list. Voiding, merging duplicates, and impersonating a registrant's portal view are all available inline, so you can resolve data problems and verify the attendee experience without switching tools or contacting support.

entries.title: Control who sees each add-on and automatically apply linked fees in Tickets
entries.summary: **Tickets › Add-ons** now supports **Who is offered this** — up to five conditions (registrant type, ticket, member status/category/level, group order, or a form answer) that together determine which registrants see the add-on. The rule is displayed as a plain sentence beneath the add-on row (e.g. "Offered only when the registrant is a member and the member level is Gold."). A new **Linked fees** panel lets organizers define fees that are added automatically to every qualifying order — scoped by ticket, add-on, or registrant type — charged once per order, per registrant, or per item, with optional promo-code bypass, price tiers, GL code, and tax rate.

enable.path: Get started → Early Access → Preview → Registration (Tickets page only)

where.path: Registration → Tickets → Add-ons (Who is offered this); Registration → Tickets → Linked fees

entries.use_case: Use add-on rules to surface member-only extras or workshop upgrades only to the registrants who qualify, reducing confusion at checkout. Use linked fees to automatically collect mandatory charges — such as a facility fee or processing surcharge — without relying on registrants to add them manually.

cs_action.note: Both features depend on the companion API PR (sessionboard-web-api#4814) being live first — do not surface to customers until both are deployed.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer asks how to restrict add-ons to members or specific ticket holders, or needs to enforce a mandatory surcharge on every order.
internal.who_should_get_it: Events with tiered membership pricing, mandatory facility or processing fees, or add-ons that should only appear for certain registrant types.
internal.staff_path: Registration → Tickets (requires Registration Early Access gate to be on for the event).

draft.docs_gap: The guide should add a section covering add-on eligibility rules (conditions, sentence preview, save behaviour) and the new Linked fees panel (scope options, per-order/per-registrant/per-item charging, promo-code bypass toggle).
draft.why_use_it: Tickets lets you define every fee, add-on, and surcharge in one place so your registration form presents the right options to the right people. Add-on rules keep irrelevant choices off the screen for registrants who do not qualify, and linked fees ensure mandatory charges are applied consistently across every order without extra steps for the registrant or your team.

entries.title: Control which add-ons registrants see, and automatically attach fees to orders
entries.summary: Two new capabilities for registration add-ons and fees. **Add-on visibility rules** let organizers show or hide an add-on based on registrant type, ticket type, membership status/category/level, group status, or a custom attendee question — up to five conditions that must all hold. A hidden add-on cannot be purchased through the public checkout or the attendee portal; staff placing orders on behalf of registrants are not restricted. **Linked fees** are a new ticket type (**Linked fee**) that the server automatically adds to qualifying orders — by order, seat, or item — without the buyer being able to add or remove them. Linked fees appear as their own order line with their own GL code, tax class, capacity, and count tiers; payment plans, invoices, and promo codes treat them like any other line (unless the fee opts out of discounts).

where.path: Registration → Tickets & Pricing → Add-ons (visibility rules); Registration → Tickets & Pricing → Linked fees

entries.use_case: Use add-on visibility rules to surface member-only extras only to members, or workshop seats only to certain registrant types — keeping the checkout clean for everyone else. Use linked fees to automatically attach mandatory processing charges, per-seat levies, or association dues to the right orders without relying on registrants to add them manually.

cs_action.note: Both features are part of the Registration beta (wave 1, agent 2). Confirm the customer's Registration feature flag is on before walking through setup. Linked fees require a ticket type of type 'linked_fee' to be configured; they are not surfaced through the standard ticket UI yet — confirm UI availability before demoing.

internal.when_to_bring_up: Any Registration beta customer who needs member-only add-ons, conditional extras, or mandatory fees that must attach automatically to orders.
internal.who_should_get_it: Organizations on the Registration beta with complex pricing rules — associations with membership tiers, events with mandatory levies, or multi-track events with type-specific workshops.
internal.staff_path: Registration → Tickets & Pricing
internal.gotchas: Staff on-behalf orders bypass add-on visibility rules (by design, matching form-window behaviour). Linked fees cannot be added or removed by the buyer; posting one as a regular add-on returns a 409. Add-on orders placed after initial registration carry 'with_items' linked fees only — fees already charged on the first order are not re-applied. Integration tests show 12 of 15 failing on main at merge time — confirm stability before customer demos.
internal.talk_track: You set the rule once on the add-on or fee, and the checkout enforces it automatically — members see member pricing, mandatory charges attach without the registrant touching them, and your finance team gets clean line items with the right GL codes.

draft.docs_gap: The /registration/tickets-and-pricing guide should add sections covering how to configure add-on visibility rules (conditions, operators, and the up-to-five-condition limit) and how to create and configure a Linked fee ticket type (applies/per settings, discountability, and how it appears on invoices and payment plans).
draft.why_use_it: Registration add-on rules and linked fees give organizers precise control over what each registrant sees and what they are charged. Visibility rules reduce checkout confusion by showing add-ons only to the people eligible for them, while linked fees ensure mandatory charges — such as processing levies, per-seat surcharges, or association dues — are applied consistently and cannot be skipped. Together they let you model complex pricing structures without manual intervention on every order.

entries.title: Registration: orders, payments, invoices, refunds, credits, payment plans, cancellation policy and finance reports
entries.summary: Adds a full financial layer to Registration (Early Access). Organizers can **Charge Card** on behalf of a registrant, record offline payments (check, cash, wire, money order, PO), issue and void **Credits**, set up **Payment Plans** with automatic installment billing, define a **Cancellation Policy** with deadlines, penalties and credit offers, process gateway or offline **Refunds**, track **Refunds to Issue** for check/PO payers, let registrants self-cancel from the manage link or Site, change or substitute a ticket (with re-pricing and a difference charge or refund), and download seven **Finance Reports** (failed transactions, GL transactions, reconciliation, AR aging, PO, promo-code usage, GL summary) as JSON or CSV. Tax settings gain a per-fee **Tax Class**, optional **VAT ID** capture with format validation, EU reverse-charge support, and VAT facts frozen on printed invoices and statements.

enable.path: Get started → Early Access → Preview → Registration

where.path: Registration → Orders; Registration → Finance; Registration → Settings → Payments

entries.use_case: Events that collect registration fees need to charge cards on behalf of attendees, handle installment billing, issue refunds through their payment gateway, and produce reconciliation-ready finance reports — all without leaving Sessionboard. Cancellation policies and self-service cancellation reduce manual work when attendees need to cancel or transfer their registration.

cs_action.note: All functionality sits behind the Registration Early Access gate. Avalara is listed as unavailable and cannot be selected — do not promise it. Payment permissions (who may charge or refund) are not yet scoped per role; any event member can charge or refund (wave 3, SB-10163/SB-10194).

internal.when_to_bring_up: Any Registration Early Access customer who collects fees, needs installment billing, or has asked for cancellation policies or finance exports.
internal.who_should_get_it: Events charging registration fees, especially those with complex tax requirements (VAT/EU), instalment plans, or finance teams needing GL-level exports.
internal.staff_path: Registration → Orders (Charge Card, Credits, Refunds); Registration → Finance (Reports, Refunds to Issue); Registration → Settings → Payments (Payment Plans, Cancellation Policy, Tax/VAT).
internal.gotchas: Avalara adapter is built but blocked (no account) — it appears as unavailable in the UI and is never called. Permission scoping for charge/refund is wave 3; currently any event member can perform financial actions. ACH payments via Spreedly bank-account tokens remain pending until the webhook settles. Idempotency keys on charges mean replaying a failed request returns the recorded attempt rather than re-charging.
internal.talk_track: Registration now handles the full payment lifecycle: charge a card on behalf of a registrant, set up a payment plan with automatic retries, apply your cancellation policy automatically, and pull a reconciliation or GL report at month-end — all on the order record.

draft.docs_gap: The guide should document all seven finance report types, the cancellation-policy configuration steps, the payment-plan admin panel (charge now / autopay / replace method), VAT ID capture modes, EU reverse charge, the Refunds to Issue workflow for check/PO payers, and the ticket-change / move-to-another-event flows introduced by this release.
draft.why_use_it: Registration finance keeps every charge, refund, credit and installment on the order record so your team always has a single source of truth. Payment plans let attendees spread the cost of attendance while the platform handles retries and redaction automatically. Cancellation policies enforce your rules consistently and give attendees a clear, self-service path to cancel or transfer, reducing support requests. Finance reports export GL-split transactions, AR aging and reconciliation data in the format your accounting team needs.
