Tokens are scoped so each integration only accesses the data it needs, and every call is tied to a specific event for clean data separation.

entries.title: Registration privacy: consent questions on the form, DPO contact, and consent withdrawal in the attendee portal
entries.summary: The registration review step now shows each of the event's configured consent questions as a checkbox; required questions keep **Next** disabled until ticked, and every answer (given or declined) is recorded in the consent log. In **Full GDPR** mode the form also displays the event's data-processing wording and a **"Questions about your data? Contact our Data Protection Officer"** line. After registering, a new **Your privacy** panel on the attendee portal **Home** tab lists each consent with its wording version and date; a **Withdraw** button appears on any consent still given, and withdrawing a consent (e.g. marketing or SMS) immediately stops the corresponding channel. The panel is hidden in staff view-as mode and for registrations managed by an external vendor.

enable.path: Event Settings → Privacy → Privacy Mode → Full GDPR; add consent questions and a DPO under Settings → Privacy

where.path: Registration form (review step) and Attendee portal → Home → Your privacy

entries.use_case: Use this when your event must comply with GDPR or similar privacy regulations: registrants explicitly consent to each data-use purpose at the point of registration, and they can withdraw individual consents at any time from their attendee portal without contacting your team.

cs_action.note: Consent questions and Full GDPR mode must be configured in Event Settings → Privacy before anything appears on the form or portal. The feature is gated behind the Registration beta; events on basic mode or without consent questions configured see no change.

internal.when_to_bring_up: Any customer running registration who mentions GDPR, data privacy compliance, or consent management for email/SMS marketing.
internal.who_should_get_it: Events with EU attendees or any organization that needs a documented consent log per registrant; especially medical, legal, and association customers.
internal.staff_path: Event Settings → Privacy → Privacy Mode and Consent Questions
internal.gotchas: The Your privacy panel is hidden when the API returns no privacy block (older API or basic mode) and when the registration is managed by an external vendor. Staff view-as shows the panel as read-only with no Withdraw button.
internal.talk_track: Registrants tick each consent purpose on the form — marketing, SMS, data processing — and the log captures both given and declined. If someone changes their mind, they withdraw from their own portal and the channel stops immediately, with the log updated automatically.

draft.docs_gap: The /registration/privacy guide should document the new consent questions setup steps, the DPO field, how the Your privacy panel appears in the attendee portal, and how registrants withdraw individual consents.
draft.why_use_it: Registration privacy gives registrants clear, granular control over how their data is used — at the moment they sign up and throughout the event lifecycle. Consent questions appear on the registration form so each purpose (marketing, SMS, data processing) is agreed to explicitly, and every answer is logged with its wording version. The attendee portal's **Your privacy** panel lets registrants review and withdraw individual consents on their own, keeping your consent log accurate without manual admin work.

entries.title: Org contacts bulk Edit now enabled for Contacts MANAGE permission
entries.summary: In the org Contacts grid, the **Edit** bulk action is now enabled for roles that have the Contacts **Manage** permission, not only those with Contacts **Update**. Previously, a role with Manage but not Update could edit a contact's field inline but saw **Edit** greyed out in the bulk actions bar with a tooltip reading "Update Contacts". Roles with only Contacts **Read** still see **Edit** disabled.

where.path: Contacts → select contacts → Edit (bulk actions bar)

entries.use_case: Teams that assign the Contacts Manage permission to roles like Program Manager can now bulk-edit org contact fields without also granting Contacts Update — matching the permission already applied to inline cell editing.

cs_action.note: Behaviour change is automatic; no configuration needed. Roles with Manage-only and no Read still cannot see rows in the grid, so the practical impact is Manage+Read roles.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer reports that a role with Contacts Manage cannot use the bulk Edit action on org contacts, or when discussing org role permission design.
internal.who_should_get_it: Any org using custom roles that grant Contacts Manage without Contacts Update — common for Program Manager-style roles.
internal.staff_path: Org → Contacts grid → select contacts → bulk actions bar → Edit
internal.gotchas: A role with Contacts Manage but no Contacts Read cannot see any rows in the org Contacts grid (the grid endpoint requires Read), so the Edit button being enabled is only meaningful for Manage+Read roles. Roles with Read only still see Edit disabled.
internal.talk_track: If you have a role that can manage individual contact fields inline but couldn't bulk-edit, that inconsistency is now resolved — Manage permission unlocks bulk Edit just as it does inline editing.

draft.docs_gap: The bulk-edit-fields guide should note that the org contacts bulk Edit action requires Contacts Update or Manage (not Update alone), and that selecting all matching records resolves to explicit record IDs rather than a query.
draft.why_use_it: Bulk editing lets you update a field across many org contacts at once without opening each record. Use it when you need to set a tier, flag, or custom attribute on a group of speakers or contacts after filtering or selecting them in the grid.

entries.title: Registration staff permissions and secure gateway management with step-up verification
entries.summary: Registration now enforces six granular permission slugs — **Money**, **Manage**, **Settings**, **Onsite**, **Finance Reports**, and a dedicated **Registration Finance** role — so event team members only see and act on what their role allows. Buttons for refunds, credits, charges, cancellations, badge design, print stations and more are disabled with a tooltip explaining the missing permission when a staff member lacks access. Payment gateway actions (**Add**, **Edit**, **Test Connection**, **Archive**) are restricted to users with **can_manage_gateways**; any sensitive gateway change — including saving a gateway assignment on **Registration Settings** — triggers a **step-up verification** dialog that requires a one-time code from an authenticator app or email before the action proceeds.

where.path: Registration → Orders / Registrants / Finance / Onsite; Event Team → Permissions → Registration; Registration → Settings → Payment

entries.use_case: Use Registration roles to give finance staff access to refunds and credits without letting them change registration settings or badge designs, and to ensure that anyone who touches payment gateway configuration must verify their identity with a second factor — reducing the risk of accidental or unauthorized changes.

cs_action.note: Permissions are UI-enforced now but the API gate (web-api#4878) must also be deployed before the UI restrictions are fully secure. Until the API is deployed, the UI ships ahead and everything stays enabled for all staff — the API remains the authoritative gate. Confirm API deployment status before telling customers the feature is live.

internal.when_to_bring_up: Any Registration customer who has multiple staff members with different responsibilities — finance, onsite, settings — or who has asked about limiting who can issue refunds or change payment gateways.
internal.who_should_get_it: All Registration (beta) customers, especially those with larger event teams or strict financial controls.
internal.staff_path: Event Team → Permissions → Registration group; Registration Finance role appears automatically on Registration events.
internal.gotchas: The Registration Finance role and the six permission slugs only appear in the roles editor when the event has Registration enabled. Users without 2FA enrolled who trigger a gateway step-up are redirected to Account Settings to enroll before they can proceed.
internal.talk_track: You can now give your finance team access to refunds and credits without letting them touch gateway settings, and anyone who changes a payment gateway has to verify with a second factor — so your payment configuration is protected even if a password is compromised.

draft.docs_gap: The guide should document all six Registration permission slugs (Money, Manage, Settings, Onsite, Finance Reports) with a table of which actions each controls, explain the Registration Finance role defaults, and describe the step-up verification flow for gateway management including the 2FA enrollment requirement.
draft.why_use_it: Registration permissions let you scope each team member's access to exactly the actions their job requires — money operations, order management, settings, onsite tools, or finance reporting — without granting blanket admin rights. The dedicated Registration Finance role makes it straightforward to give finance staff the access they need while keeping gateway and settings controls in the hands of administrators. Step-up verification adds a second layer of protection for the most sensitive gateway actions, so a compromised session cannot silently redirect payments.

entries.title: Registration gets its own permission set, a Finance role, and MFA-gated payment gateway management
entries.summary: **Event Team › Permissions › Registration** now shows six granular permissions — **View registrations**, **Manage registrations**, **Take payments and issue refunds**, **View finance reports**, **Manage settings**, and **Manage onsite** — on any event with Registration turned on. A stock **Registration Finance** role (view + payments + finance reports) is seeded for every Registration event. A new org-level permission **Manage payment gateways** controls who can add, edit, archive, test-charge or test-connect a gateway; changing an event's gateway in Registration settings requires the same permission. Any action that touches a payment gateway also requires a **recent second factor** (verified within 15 minutes); admins without 2FA enrolled are prompted to set it up, and a new step-up flow lets enrolled admins re-verify without signing out.

where.path: Event Team → Permissions → Registration (per event); Organization Settings → Payments (gateway management)

entries.use_case: Give finance staff the ability to charge, refund and view reports without letting them change ticket types or badge templates. Lock down payment gateway changes to org admins who have recently verified a second factor, so credentials are never touched by accident or by a compromised session.

cs_action.note: All existing event roles were seeded with the permissions they already had in practice (most get view + manage + payments + finance reports; roles with Settings update also get settings + onsite; Evaluator and Portal User get none; Reporting Only Admin gets view + finance reports; Read-Only User gets view). Org Admins and any org role with Settings update get Manage payment gateways. No one loses access on deploy. Event-only admins can no longer pick the event's gateway — this is intentional and had zero real-world impact at deploy time (no live Registration events in US or EU). Review any customer who has event-only admins managing gateways.

internal.when_to_bring_up: Any Registration customer who wants to give finance staff refund access without full admin rights, or who asks about locking down payment gateway changes.
internal.who_should_get_it: All Registration (beta) customers; especially those with separate finance, onsite, or settings teams.
internal.staff_path: Event Team → Permissions → Registration; Organization Settings → Payments → Gateways
internal.gotchas: The MFA step-up expires after 15 minutes. SSO users pass automatically (IdP owns the factor). Impersonation is blocked on all gateway and step-up routes. The Registration Finance role appears in permission profiles and event roles only on Registration events. CFP, Awards and Lessons gateway pickers are not yet gated by the new org permission — follow-up tickets exist.
internal.talk_track: You can now give your finance team exactly what they need — charge, refund, and report — without handing them the keys to your ticket setup or badge templates. And anyone who touches your payment gateway has to prove who they are with a fresh second factor every 15 minutes.

draft.docs_gap: The article /registration/roles-and-permissions does not yet exist and should be created to document all six permissions, the Registration Finance stock role, the Manage payment gateways org permission, and the MFA step-up requirement for gateway actions.
draft.why_use_it: Registration permissions let you match each team member's access to their actual job: a finance coordinator can process refunds and pull revenue reports without touching event settings or badge designs, while an onsite manager can print badges without seeing payment data. The **Registration Finance** role is ready to assign the moment you turn Registration on, so you do not have to build it from scratch. Gateway management is separated from day-to-day registration work and protected by a step-up second factor, so payment credentials stay under the control of the people who own them.

entries.title: Attendee portal shows seating assignment and flags externally managed registrations
entries.summary: The attendee portal **Home** tab now displays a **Your table** panel showing the registrant's seating plan, room, table, seat number, sponsor and host — pulled from the seating plan when "show in portal" is enabled. Registrations held in another platform (such as Cvent) show a notice that the registration is managed externally and become read-only: the fieldset is disabled and **Cancel**, **Transfer** and **Add-ons** actions are hidden. Content Gallery items restricted to the new **Registrants only** access mode show a "For registered attendees" gate and a **Registrants only** lock label to non-registered visitors.

enable.path: Registration → Seating → [plan] → Show in portal (to surface the table panel); Content Galleries → Access → Registrants only (to gate gallery content)

where.path: Attendee portal → Home tab (Your table panel); Content Gallery (Registrants only gate)

entries.use_case: Attendees can see exactly where they are sitting without contacting the event team. When registration is managed in Cvent or another platform, the portal surfaces the record read-only so attendees have their details without risking conflicting edits. Gating Content Gallery content to registered attendees lets organizers reward registration with exclusive session recordings or materials.

cs_action.note: Three distinct changes ship together: the seating panel (requires 'show in portal' on the seating plan), the external-registration read-only notice (automatic when managed_in is set, e.g. Cvent), and the Content Gallery 'registrants' access mode gate. Confirm with customers using Cvent that the read-only behaviour matches their expectations before promoting.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When talking to customers who use seating plans, sync registrations from Cvent or another platform, or want to gate Content Gallery content to registered attendees.
internal.who_should_get_it: Events using Registration (beta) with seating plans, Cvent or similar integrations, or Content Galleries with attendee-only content.
internal.staff_path: Registration → Seating → plan settings; Registration → Integrations; Content Galleries → Access
internal.gotchas: The seating panel is hidden when the plan's 'show in portal' toggle is off. The external-registration notice and read-only state are driven by the managed_in field on the registration record — this must be set by the integration sync. The API returns 409 managed_externally if a client attempts cancel, transfer or add-on actions on an externally managed registration.
internal.talk_track: Attendees see their table assignment right in the portal, and if their registration lives in Cvent we show it read-only so nothing gets out of sync. You can also lock down your Content Gallery recordings to registered attendees only.

draft.docs_gap: The attendee-portal guide should document the Your table panel (what fields appear, the show-in-portal toggle), the externally-managed registration notice and its read-only behaviour, and the Registrants only Content Gallery access mode.
draft.why_use_it: The attendee portal gives registrants a single place to view their registration details, seating assignment, and event content — all without staff intervention. Use it to reduce inbound questions about table assignments, protect data integrity when a third-party platform owns the registration record, and deliver gated content only to people who have registered.

entries.title: Seat registrants at tables, print table tents, and connect external registration vendors
entries.summary: Two new capabilities ship together under Registration. **Table Seating**: create a seating plan, add tables, and seat registrants manually or automatically (by group order, company, or name); voided or canceled registrants drop out automatically. Print **Table Tents**, folded place cards, flat place cards, a seating chart, per-table lists (PDF), and a CSV. Registrants see their table assignment in the attendee portal. **External Registration Vendors**: registrations held in Maritz RTS, Stova, Grip, Eventbrite, RainFocus, Brella, or ASP flow in through the Apps Engine and appear in the attendee portal as read-only records (labeled **Managed in [vendor]**); organizers control which sources count as live registrations via **Registration → Access**. A new **Content Gallery** access mode (**Registrants**) gates gallery viewing on a valid registration from any configured source.

enable.path: Ask your Customer Success Manager to enable Registration; then Event → Registration → Seating for table plans, and Event → Registration → Access for vendor source rules.

where.path: Registration → Seating; Registration → Access; Content Galleries → Access (Registrants mode); Attendee portal → My Registration (table assignment)

entries.use_case: Use table seating to assign and print place cards for gala dinners, award banquets, or any seated meal without leaving Sessionboard. Use the external-vendor access rules to give attendees registered in Maritz RTS, Stova, Eventbrite, or another supported platform a unified portal experience and gate content galleries on a valid registration from any source.

cs_action.note: Both table seating and external-vendor access are behind feature--registration, which must be enabled per event. External vendor connectors also require the relevant Apps Engine connector to be set up and mapped.

internal.when_to_bring_up: Any customer running a seated dinner, awards banquet, or gala alongside their conference, or any customer whose attendees register in Maritz RTS, Stova, Grip, Eventbrite, RainFocus, Brella, or ASP and who wants those attendees in the Sessionboard portal.
internal.who_should_get_it: Events with Registration enabled that have seated meal functions; events using a third-party registration platform that want a unified attendee portal or gated content galleries.
internal.staff_path: Event → Registration → Seating (table plans); Event → Registration → Access (vendor source rules).
internal.gotchas: External registrations are read-only in the portal — attendees cannot edit, cancel, transfer, or add on from Sessionboard. The Content Gallery Registrants access mode refuses to apply on galleries not tied to an event. Voided registrants lose their seat automatically; canceled registrants drop out of seat counts.
internal.talk_track: If your attendees register in another system, they can still get a Sessionboard portal experience and access gated content galleries — and for seated events, you can assign tables, auto-seat by company or name, and print place cards all in one place.

draft.docs_gap: The /registration/seating guide should document the auto-seat options (by group order, company, and name), the FOLD_STOCKS place-card stock types, the seating chart and per-table PDF/CSV exports, and the attendee portal table-assignment display. The /registration/integrations-and-api guide should document the Registration → Access settings (mode: any vs. mode: rule), the list of supported external vendors, the managed_in read-only portal state, and the Content Gallery Registrants access mode.
draft.why_use_it: Registration brings attendee management — ticketing, seating, portal access, and content gating — into the same platform where you manage your program. Table seating lets you assign, move, and print place cards from a single plan that stays in sync as registrations change. External-vendor support means attendees registered anywhere can still sign in to the attendee portal and access gated content, so you are not forced to choose between your registration system and your event experience.

entries.title: Fix: `{{{subsessions_summary}}}` merge tag now renders cell padding, blank empty cells, and escaped titles correctly
entries.summary: The **`{{{subsessions_summary}}}`** email merge tag had three rendering bugs now corrected: table cells were missing their padding because the CSS `style` attribute was malformed (`style="style=…"`); subsession ID cells printed `SB-100-null` or `undefined-100-1` when a friendly ID or record prefix was absent; and subsession titles from CFP submitters were inserted into the email body without HTML escaping, so characters like `&` or `<` could break the layout. All three are fixed — cells now have visible padding, missing IDs and times show as blank, and special characters in titles render literally.

where.path: Sessions → select a session → Send Email; Email Campaigns → campaign body using {{{subsessions_summary}}}

entries.use_case: Organizers who send session emails or email campaigns containing a subsession summary table will now see correctly spaced rows, blank cells where data is missing, and safe rendering of any special characters in subsession titles — without any configuration change.

cs_action.note: Fix is automatic — no action needed. All 103 previously sent emails that contained the broken style attribute will not be retroactively corrected, but any new send or campaign using {{{subsessions_summary}}} will render correctly.

internal.when_to_bring_up: If a customer reports that their subsession summary table looks cramped, shows 'null' or 'undefined' in ID cells, or that HTML tags in a subsession title appear as raw text in emails.
internal.who_should_get_it: Any event using Send Email or Email Campaigns with the {{{subsessions_summary}}} merge tag — roughly 15 events/orgs across US and EU prod as of 2026-10-28.
internal.gotchas: Previously sent emails (77 US + 26 EU campaign emails) already contain the broken markup and cannot be retroactively fixed. The column structure and data source are unchanged — only rendering correctness is affected.
internal.talk_track: The subsession summary table in your emails now shows proper cell spacing, leaves blank any missing IDs or times instead of printing 'null', and safely displays any special characters in subsession titles.

draft.docs_gap: The email campaigns merge tags reference should document {{{subsessions_summary}}} explicitly, including what each column shows, how missing values appear, and how HTML in titles is handled.
draft.why_use_it: null

entries.title: Registration portal: autopay placement, linked-fee payment prompt, substitution timing, and view-as error recovery
entries.summary: Several attendee-facing registration portal behaviours are corrected: the **Waitlist Autopay** panel now appears only on the Home page (not on every page); a failed autopay status load shows an error with a **Try again** option instead of silently hiding the panel; a registration type with a positive **linked fee** now correctly prompts for payment; the **Send to a colleague** substitution option is hidden while transfer terms are still loading; and the **View as** error page now shows **Exit view as** and **Try again** buttons when a view-as link has expired.

where.path: Attendee portal → Home; Registration flow → Payment step; Registration flow → Transfer / Send to a colleague

entries.use_case: Attendees registering or managing their registration see consistent, accurate prompts — they are not asked to pay when nothing is owed, not shown a substitution option before terms have loaded, and can recover cleanly when a view-as session expires.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer reports that autopay appears on multiple portal pages, that a linked-fee registration type does not trigger payment, or that the substitution option appears before terms load.
internal.who_should_get_it: Any event using registration with autopay, linked fees, or substitutions enabled.
internal.gotchas: The view-as token expiry fix only applies to the org-portal web client; server-side token validation is unchanged.
internal.talk_track: A handful of edge cases in the attendee portal — duplicate autopay panels, a missing payment prompt on linked-fee types, a premature substitution option, and a dead-end error on expired view-as links — are all resolved in this release.

draft.docs_gap: The attendee-portal guide should note that the Waitlist Autopay panel appears on the Home page only, and describe the recovery options (Exit view as / Try again) shown when a view-as link expires.
draft.why_use_it: The attendee portal lets registrants view their order, pay a balance, add workshops or extras, and transfer their registration to a colleague — all without contacting the event team. Keeping these flows accurate reduces support requests and gives attendees confidence that what they see reflects their real registration state.

entries.title: Registration form: SMS opt-in for registrants
entries.summary: When an event has SMS enabled, the registration form's review step now shows the organizer's consent text as an **SMS opt-in** checkbox. Checking it reveals a mobile number field (E.164 format); **Next** waits for a valid number before proceeding. The registrant's opt-in choice and phone number are submitted at checkout.

where.path: Registration → Forms → [form] → Review step

entries.use_case: Collect explicit SMS consent and a verified mobile number at the point of registration, so you can send text reminders and updates only to attendees who have opted in.

cs_action.note: Appears automatically on the review step when the event has SMS enabled; no manual toggle required.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer asks how to grow their SMS opt-in list or wants to collect mobile numbers during registration.
internal.who_should_get_it: Any customer using Registration (beta) who also sends SMS communications to attendees.
internal.gotchas: The opt-in checkbox and mobile field only render when the event's registration form returns sms: non-null from the API. Events without SMS configured will not see the field. The E.164 phone validator is a minimal inline check; a more robust library (SB-10133) is planned.
internal.talk_track: Attendees see your consent language as a checkbox at checkout and enter their mobile number right there — you get a clean, opted-in SMS list without any extra steps.

draft.docs_gap: The Registration forms guide should document the SMS opt-in checkbox on the review step, including how to configure the consent text and what data is captured at checkout.
draft.why_use_it: The registration form's SMS opt-in lets attendees choose to receive text messages from your event at the moment they register, pairing consent with a validated mobile number in one step. This keeps your SMS list compliant and accurate without a separate follow-up form or manual data entry.

entries.title: Registration: organizer notifications for registration events and opt-in SMS for registrants
entries.summary: Organizers can now configure **Admin Notifications** (under Registration settings) to receive email or Slack alerts — instantly or as a daily digest — when registrations are created, changed, cancelled, voided, waitlisted, or pending approval, with optional filters by registrant type, ticket, and form. Registrants can opt in to SMS at checkout (**SMS Opt-In** + phone number in E.164 format); organizers can send SMS reminders and onsite notices to opted-in attendees, and Twilio STOP/START replies are handled automatically.

enable.path: Registration → Settings → Notifications (for admin alerts); Registration → Settings → SMS (to enable opt-in SMS for registrants)

where.path: Registration → Settings → Notifications; Registration → Settings → SMS; Registration → Registrants (SMS opt-in shown on registrant record)

entries.use_case: Keep your registration team informed in real time — or via a daily digest — without logging in to check the queue. Let registrants opt in to SMS so you can reach them with reminders and onsite notices directly on their phones.

cs_action.note: SMS requires Twilio number webhooks to be pointed at the API inbound endpoint and US A2P 10DLC campaign registration before production texting. Coordinate with engineering before enabling SMS for any customer. Admin notifications are self-serve once Registration is on.

internal.when_to_bring_up: Any Registration customer who asks about real-time alerts, Slack notifications, or texting attendees before or during the event.
internal.who_should_get_it: Events with active registration teams monitoring sign-ups, waitlists, or approvals; events that want to send SMS reminders or onsite notices to attendees.
internal.staff_path: Registration → Settings → Notifications; Registration → Settings → SMS
internal.gotchas: SMS is gated behind Twilio number configuration and 10DLC campaign approval — do not promise SMS to customers until those deploy steps are confirmed. The SMS credit balance uses the Emails meter; monitor limits. Non-production environments only text @sessionboard.com / @lennd.com addresses. Daily SMS cap per event is 5,000.
internal.talk_track: Your team gets a Slack ping or email the moment someone registers, cancels, or hits the waitlist — no more checking the dashboard. And for attendees who opt in at checkout, you can text them reminders and day-of updates so nothing gets buried in their inbox.

draft.docs_gap: The guide should add a section covering the new Admin Notifications settings (triggers, filters, destinations, instant vs. digest delivery) and a section on SMS opt-in setup, the checkout experience, sending SMS reminders and onsite notices, and managing opt-outs.
draft.why_use_it: Registration admin notifications let your team react immediately to new sign-ups, cancellations, waitlist additions, and approvals without polling the registrant list. SMS opt-in gives registrants a way to receive reminders and onsite updates by text, reaching them even when email goes unread. Together they close the gap between what happens in registration and what your team and attendees know about it.

entries.title: Weekly portal summary email now sends when any item is open, not only required ones
entries.summary: The scheduled **Weekly digest email** (portal task summary) now keeps sending to a participant as long as they have **any** outstanding item — a task, an unsubmitted form, or an unsubmitted or denied file request — whether that item is marked required or optional. Previously, if a participant had completed all required items but still had optional items open, the email stopped. The **Run dry run** preview in **Portals → Weekly reminders** reflects the same logic, so the list of recipients shown there matches who will actually receive the next scheduled send.

enable.path: Portals → [portal name] → Configuration → Weekly digest email → on

where.path: Portals → Weekly reminders → Run dry run

entries.use_case: Participants who still have optional tasks, forms, or file requests outstanding will continue to receive weekly reminders until everything is done — so nothing slips through because it was not marked required.

cs_action.note: Behaviour change ships automatically with the next API release. No configuration needed.

internal.when_to_bring_up: Any customer asking why speakers with optional items open stopped receiving weekly reminders, or why the dry-run list seemed too short.
internal.who_should_get_it: All customers using the weekly portal digest email with a mix of required and optional portal items.
internal.staff_path: Portals → Weekly reminders → Run dry run (shows the updated recipient list)
internal.gotchas: The fix affects all three surfaces together: the Monday cron, the dry-run preview, and the per-contact dry-run 'Send now'. The targeted 'Send portal summary' from Contacts / Accounts always sends regardless of completion status — that is unchanged. Participants whose every item is complete, approved, or pending admin review are still skipped.
internal.talk_track: Before this fix, a participant who finished all their required items but still had an optional task or file request open would stop getting weekly reminders. Now the email keeps coming until everything is done, so optional items don't get forgotten.

draft.docs_gap: The guide should explain that the scheduled weekly digest email sends whenever a participant has any outstanding item (required or optional) — an open task, an unsubmitted form, or an unsubmitted or denied file request — and stops only when all items are complete, approved, or pending admin review; it should also note that a comment on the participant's sessions in the last 7 days triggers a send, and that the manual "Send portal summary" action always sends regardless of completion status.
draft.why_use_it: The weekly portal digest keeps participants moving through their to-do list without manual follow-up from the event team. It sends automatically each week to anyone with open items and stops only when a participant has nothing left to do — every task complete, every form submitted, and every file approved or pending review. Use it alongside tasks, forms, and file requests to drive completion rates without writing individual reminder emails.

entries.title: Sessions summary email tag: empty cells no longer show "undefined" or "null", and cell padding now applies
entries.summary: Two display defects in the **{{{sessions_summary}}}** merge tag table are fixed. Sessions with no status or no speakers now render a blank cell instead of the words "undefined" or "null". where.path: Contacts → Send Email (body: {{{sessions_summary}}}); Email Campaigns → campaign body

entries.use_case: Organizers who email speakers or contacts a summary of their sessions no longer need to worry about "undefined" or "null" appearing in the Status or Speakers columns when a session has no value set for those fields.

internal.when_to_bring_up: If a customer reports seeing 'undefined' or 'null' in a sessions summary email, or notices the table has no visible padding — both are fixed automatically.
internal.who_should_get_it: Any organizer using the {{{sessions_summary}}} merge tag in Send Email or Email Campaigns.

internal.talk_track: The sessions summary table in emails now shows blank cells for missing status or speakers, and the padding renders correctly in all email clients including Outlook.

entries.title: Configure hotel housing hand-off and see who booked from Registration
entries.summary: A **Housing** panel in **Registration › Integrations & API** lets organizers connect a hotel booking provider (Passkey, Orchid, onPeak, or custom), set a booking link with merge fields, customize button text, toggle confirmation page and email prompts, and copy a signed webhook URL with **Show secret** / **Make a new secret** controls. Once a provider sends a status back, a **Housing** line (status, hotel, dates, reference) appears on each registrant's drawer and the **Who booked** table shows booked, cancelled, and not-yet counts per registrant.

where.path: Registration → Integrations & API → Housing; Registration → Registrants (drawer → Housing)

entries.use_case: Events that block hotel rooms through Passkey, Orchid, onPeak, or a custom provider can now send registrants directly to the booking link and track who has booked, cancelled, or not yet acted — all without leaving Registration.

cs_action.note: Feature is part of Registration (beta). Confirm the customer's housing provider is one of the four supported options (Passkey, Orchid, onPeak, custom) before walking them through setup. The webhook secret must be shared with the provider — use Show secret / Make a new secret in the panel.

internal.when_to_bring_up: Any Registration beta customer whose event has a contracted hotel block or uses a housing bureau.
internal.who_should_get_it: Conferences and association events that manage room blocks through Passkey, Orchid, or onPeak.
internal.staff_path: Registration → Integrations & API → Housing
internal.gotchas: Status updates only appear on the registrant drawer after the housing provider has sent at least one webhook payload. The public form and confirmation-page side of this feature shipped in a companion PR (lennd/sessionboard-web-org-portal#246); both sides are needed for the full flow.
internal.talk_track: Registrants get a one-click path to your hotel block, and you can see at a glance who has booked, who cancelled, and who still needs a nudge — all inside Registration.

draft.docs_gap: The /registration/housing guide should document the four supported providers, how to configure merge fields in the booking link, how to set up and rotate the webhook secret, and what the registrant-facing confirmation page and email switches control.
draft.why_use_it: Housing hand-off connects your registration flow to your contracted hotel block so registrants reach the booking page in one click, pre-identified by merge fields. The admin side shows live booking status for every registrant — booked, cancelled, or not yet — so your team can follow up without exporting data to a spreadsheet. Webhook-based status updates from the housing provider flow back automatically and appear on each registrant's record.

entries.title: Send registrants to your hotel booking partner and validate international addresses and phone numbers at checkout
entries.summary: Two new capabilities for Registration. **Housing hand-off**: configure a hotel booking link (Passkey, Orchid, onPeak, or a custom URL) under **Registration → Housing**; confirmed registrants see a **Book your hotel** button on their confirmation page and in their confirmation email, with merge fields pre-filled from their registration record. **International validation**: phone numbers are stored in E.164 format, postal codes and regions are checked against the registrant's country, address fields that do not exist for a country (e.g. UK state, UAE postal code) are never required, and single-word or non-Latin-script names are accepted; validation error messages appear in the language of the registration form (English, Spanish, French, Arabic, German, Portuguese).

where.path: Registration → Housing (settings); Registration → Registrants (housing status column and drawer)

entries.use_case: For events with a room block, connect registrants directly to your hotel partner at the moment of confirmation — with their name, email, and registration details pre-filled — so they book in your block rather than on a third-party site. International validation means attendees from outside the US see relevant address fields and get error messages in their own language, reducing checkout abandonment and support tickets.

cs_action.note: Housing hand-off is new infrastructure. Passkey, Orchid and onPeak do not yet publish attendee prefill parameters or a status webhook format, so all three use generic query parameters and the generic signed JSON webhook. Advise customers that provider-specific deep-link prefill is not yet certified. Secret rotation is available via POST …/housing/secret with { rotate: true } and is audited.

internal.when_to_bring_up: Any event with a contracted room block or a hotel partner (Passkey, Orchid, onPeak, or custom booking page), and any event with significant international attendance.
internal.who_should_get_it: Events using Registration (beta) that have a hotel room block or international attendees.
internal.staff_path: Registration → Housing
internal.gotchas: Provider-specific prefill (e.g. Passkey RegLink/RegExpress) requires partner credentials not yet integrated — all providers fall back to generic query parameters. Housing booking status flows back via a signed webhook; the per-event secret is derived and never stored, so rotation voids the old secret immediately. International validation only applies to values written in a new request; existing stored phone numbers are not migrated.
internal.talk_track: After a registrant confirms, they see a 'Book your hotel' button pre-filled with their details — no copy-paste, no re-entry. And for your international attendees, the checkout now speaks their language and only asks for address fields that actually exist in their country.

draft.docs_gap: The /registration/housing guide should document: how to configure the URL template and available merge fields, how the webhook signature verification works (X-Sessionboard-Signature header, 5-minute window), how to rotate the signing secret, and the current limitation that Passkey/Orchid/onPeak use generic parameters pending partner certification.
draft.why_use_it: Registration's housing hand-off lets you point confirmed registrants to your contracted hotel partner immediately after they register, with their details pre-filled in the booking URL so they do not have to re-enter information. International address and phone validation ensures that registrants worldwide see only the fields relevant to their country, receive error messages in their language, and have their phone numbers stored in a consistent format — making your registrant data cleaner and your checkout experience smoother for a global audience.

entries.title: Staff can view the attendee portal as a registrant in read-only mode
entries.summary: When a staff member uses **View as registrant**, the attendee portal opens in a fully read-only state: a sticky amber banner identifies whose registration is being viewed and when the session expires, and every button and input is disabled so no changes can be made on the registrant's behalf. An expired or voided view-as link shows its own message. Closing the tab signs the staff member out of the view-as session without affecting the registrant's own portal access.

where.path: Registration → Registrants → open a registrant → View as registrant

entries.use_case: Support staff can open exactly what a registrant sees in their portal — including their order, payment plan, and add-ons — without risking accidental edits, making it faster to diagnose access or display issues during registration support calls.

internal.when_to_bring_up: Any customer using Registration who fields support requests from attendees about what they see in their portal.
internal.who_should_get_it: Events using the Registration (beta) feature where staff regularly assist registrants with portal navigation or payment issues.
internal.staff_path: Registration → Registrants → open a registrant record → View as registrant button (shipped in lennd/sessionboard-web-ui-v2#1227)
internal.gotchas: The view-as token is stored in tab-only session storage under its own key, completely separate from the registrant's own portal token — opening the link in a new tab will not bleed into an existing staff session. The API also enforces read-only at the server (non-GET requests return 403), so the client-side fieldset disabled is a second layer of protection.
internal.talk_track: Your support team can open a registrant's exact portal view — banner, balance, add-ons and all — in a time-limited read-only session, so they can see what the attendee sees without any risk of making changes.

draft.docs_gap: The /registration/registrants guide should add a "View as a registrant" section explaining how to open the view-as session, what the amber banner shows, the read-only enforcement, and how the session expires.
draft.why_use_it: The attendee portal is what registrants use to pay balances, manage add-ons, and review their registration. Being able to open that exact view as a staff member lets your team confirm what a registrant sees, reproduce reported issues, and walk someone through their portal over the phone — all without touching their record.

entries.title: Void registrations, merge duplicates, and view the portal as a registrant
entries.summary: Three new actions are available from the registrant record. **Void** removes a registration from all live counts, capacity, check-in, badge printing, and automated emails without issuing a refund — the response surfaces paid amounts so you can refund from the order if needed. **Merge duplicate** moves orders, form answers, workshop seats, check-in scans, staff notes, credits, and membership from a duplicate record onto a survivor, then voids the duplicate; a **Merge preview** shows exactly what will move before you confirm. **View as registrant** mints a 30-minute read-only session so you can open the attendee portal exactly as that person sees it — every action is audited and the token cannot be used to make changes.

where.path: Registration → Registrants → [open a registrant] → Void / Merge duplicate / View as registrant

entries.use_case: Use Void to cleanly remove a test, cancelled, or fraudulent registration without touching gateway records, and use Merge to consolidate a duplicate registrant — carrying over their orders, answers, and history — so your counts, capacity, and finance reports stay accurate. Use View as registrant to troubleshoot portal issues or confirm what an attendee sees without sharing credentials.

cs_action.note: Void requires event Contacts delete permission — reporting-only admins get a 403. View as registrant requires the Portals impersonate permission. Confirm customer role configurations include these permissions for the team members who will use these actions. A void never triggers a refund; CS should remind customers to refund from the order separately if money was collected.

internal.when_to_bring_up: Any customer dealing with duplicate registrants, test records in production, or support tickets where an organizer needs to see exactly what an attendee sees in the portal.
internal.who_should_get_it: Events using Registration (beta) with active registrant lists, especially those running paid registration where duplicate or voided records affect revenue reporting.
internal.staff_path: Registration → Registrants → open a registrant record → action menu
internal.gotchas: Void does not refund — paid_cents is returned in the API response so the UI can prompt the organizer to refund from the order. A voided registration cannot be used with View as registrant (returns 409). Merge preview and merge share the same plan, so what the preview lists is exactly what moves. Group orders keep reporting while any seat on them is live.
internal.talk_track: If you have duplicate registrants or need to retire a test record, you can now void or merge directly from the registrant record — your counts, capacity, and finance reports update immediately. And if an attendee says their portal looks wrong, you can open it as them in read-only mode to see exactly what they see.

draft.docs_gap: The /registration/registrants guide should add a dedicated section covering void (what it removes, what it keeps, the no-refund behaviour), merge (preview, what moves, money is never re-charged), and view as registrant (30-minute token, read-only, audit trail, 409 conditions) with the required permissions for each action.
draft.why_use_it: Registration records sometimes need to be retired or consolidated: a registrant submits twice, a test record slips into production, or two contacts turn out to be the same person. Voiding removes a record from every live surface — counts, capacity, check-in, badge queues, and emails — while keeping it visible in finance reconciliation. Merging carries the full history of a duplicate onto the record you want to keep, so nothing is lost. Viewing as a registrant lets you see the attendee portal through their eyes, read-only and fully audited, without needing their password.

entries.title: Registration: add-on eligibility rules, linked fees on the cart, and waitlist autopay
entries.summary: Three improvements to the registration flow. (1) **Add-ons** are now filtered by eligibility — only add-ons the registrant's seat is offered (based on registrant type, ticket, group order, form answers, and membership) appear in the add-ons step; the same rules are enforced at checkout. (2) The add-ons step and quote now show any fees that will be added automatically (e.g. "Added automatically: Shipping ($15.00)") as **linked fees**. (3) Waitlisted registrants with a paid registration can opt in to **Pay automatically when a place opens** from the attendee portal (manage link): save a card in the payment window, swap it, or turn it off; if a charge is declined the usual manual offer is sent instead.

where.path: Registration → public form (add-ons step) and Registration → attendee portal (manage link)

entries.use_case: Organizers running paid registrations with tiered add-ons or membership-gated extras no longer need to rely on registrants self-selecting correctly — ineligible add-ons are hidden automatically and blocked at checkout. Waitlisted attendees can save a card so they are charged the moment a spot opens, reducing drop-off from manual follow-up.

cs_action.note: Add-on eligibility rules (show_if) and linked fees require that add-ons and fees are configured correctly in the fee schedule; misconfigured rules will silently hide add-ons. Waitlist autopay requires a Spreedly gateway connection — confirm the gateway is live before promoting this to customers.

internal.when_to_bring_up: Any customer using paid registration with add-ons, membership pricing, or a waitlist on high-demand events.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers on the Registration beta who have add-ons with eligibility conditions or who run waitlisted paid events.
internal.staff_path: Registration → Tickets & Pricing (add-ons and linked fees config); Registration → Registrants (waitlist queue)
internal.gotchas: An add-on already in the cart before a registrant type or membership change is NOT automatically removed — it stays in the cart and is only blocked at checkout (409 addon_unavailable). Waitlist autopay card removal happens at Spreedly on opt-out; confirm gateway supports card vault operations.
internal.talk_track: Your add-ons step now only shows what each registrant can actually buy, and the total they see includes any automatic fees — no surprises at checkout. Waitlisted attendees can save a card so they are charged instantly when a spot opens, instead of waiting for a manual email.

draft.docs_gap: The tickets-and-pricing guide should add a section on add-on eligibility rules (show_if conditions), how linked fees appear in the cart and quote, and how to configure waitlist autopay for paid registrations.
draft.why_use_it: Registration lets you sell tickets, add-ons, and workshops with pricing rules tied to registrant type, membership, and form answers. Eligibility filtering keeps the cart clean by showing each registrant only what they qualify for, linked fees make the total transparent before checkout, and waitlist autopay converts waitlisted attendees into confirmed registrants without manual intervention.

entries.title: Advocacy Generate Content: speaker attribution, gallery filtering and job status now work correctly
entries.summary: Four bugs in **Marketing → Transcriptions → Generate Content** are fixed. Speaker names and contact links now appear on quote cards. The **Gallery** correctly filters by session. A job where every requested step fails is now reported as failed rather than completed, so the error is visible immediately instead of being buried in the job result.

where.path: Marketing → Transcriptions → Gallery / Generate Content

entries.use_case: Organizers who generate quote cards and recaps from session transcripts can now trust that speaker names appear on quote cards, the gallery filters correctly by session, and any generation failure surfaces immediately as an error status rather than a silent false-positive completion.

cs_action.note: All four defects are fixed server-side with no configuration required. The Amplify_Artifacts table had 0 rows in all regions before the migration ran, so no existing gallery content is affected.

internal.when_to_bring_up: Any customer who tried Generate Content and saw an empty gallery or jobs that appeared to complete successfully but produced nothing.
internal.who_should_get_it: Any event using Marketing Transcriptions / Generate Content (Advocacy).
internal.staff_path: Marketing → Transcriptions → Gallery
internal.gotchas: The contact_id column was migrated to UUID with USING NULL, so any pre-existing rows would have lost their contact link — but the table was confirmed empty in US, EU and ME before the migration ran. The session UUID filter fix means any gallery links or API calls that previously passed integer session IDs will now need to pass the correct UUID.
internal.talk_track: Generate Content now correctly attributes quote cards to the right speakers and lets you filter the gallery by session — and if something goes wrong during generation you will see a clear error instead of an empty gallery with a 'completed' status.

draft.docs_gap: The Recaps guide should note that Generate Content attributes quote cards to named speakers and that the Gallery can be filtered by session.
draft.why_use_it: null

entries.title: Webhooks get a new screen, with the reason for every failed delivery
entries.summary: Webhook endpoints are now managed on a Sessionboard screen in **Settings → Integrations → Webhooks** (one event) and **Organization Settings → Webhooks** (every event). Add an endpoint, pick event types, add custom headers, reveal or rotate the signing secret, send a test, and read the delivery log — including why a request failed, such as a DNS or certificate error. Requests keep the same payload, headers and signatures, so existing receivers need no change.

where.path: Settings → Integrations → Webhooks; Organization Settings → Webhooks

entries.use_case: Teams sending session or contact changes to a CRM or website can set up, test and troubleshoot their webhooks in Sessionboard, and see exactly why a delivery failed instead of an empty response.

cs_action.note: Customers who already had webhooks keep them on a Legacy webhooks tab next to the new screen; nothing moves. New endpoints are added on the Webhooks tab. Zapier connections need the Sessionboard Zapier app 1.2.0 once it is published.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer asks why a webhook is not arriving, how to verify signatures, or how to send changes from every event to one URL.
internal.who_should_get_it: Any customer with an integration that listens to Sessionboard changes (CRM, website, Zapier, in-house tools).
internal.staff_path: Event → Settings → Integrations → Webhooks; Organization Settings → Webhooks. Staff-only Admin Settings feature: Legacy Webhooks.
internal.gotchas: Endpoint URLs must be public https; private and internal addresses are refused on save. Custom header values are hidden after saving. A rotated secret keeps the old one valid for 24 hours. Legacy (Svix) endpoints stay on the Legacy webhooks tab for orgs and events that had them.
internal.talk_track: Webhooks now live on Sessionboard's own screen. You can test an endpoint, read its delivery log, and see the exact reason a delivery failed. Existing endpoints keep working unchanged.

entries.title: History names date formula recalculations and integration writes
entries.summary: Record History and Activity now say where a system change came from: **Date formula recalculation** when the daily job moves a date formula result, and the integration for app writes, such as **Visit writeback** or **Maritz RTS sync** (**Integration sync** when the app is unknown). Both appear only when a value actually changed, and both move the record's last-updated time forward.

where.path: History → Audit, or a contact's Activity → Audit History

entries.use_case: When a value changes overnight or arrives from a connected app, the History entry now says which job or app made the change instead of showing a blank name, and filters, search and the Public API's updated_at pick the change up.

cs_action.note: Automatic. Older system rows written before this release keep their blank name.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer asks who changed a field with no name in History, why a days-until count changed with nobody editing, or why a record's last-updated time moved after an integration sync.
internal.who_should_get_it: Events using formula fields with days_until or add_days, and events connected to apps that write values back (Visit, Maritz RTS and other Apps connectors).
internal.staff_path: Event → History → Audit; Contact → Activity → Audit History
internal.gotchas: The date formula recalculation does not fire automations or webhooks; it only updates the record's last-updated time and writes the History entry. Unchanged values write nothing, so a nightly recalculation that keeps the same result leaves no row.
internal.talk_track: Every change in History now tells you who or what made it: a person, the Public API, a bulk edit, the nightly date formula job, or the named integration.

entries.title: Report builder field names match the Sessions grid
entries.summary: Session fields in the **Report Builder** now use the Sessions grid's column names, such as **Client Session ID** (previously "External system ID"), **Starts At** and **Last Updated**. Field search also matches a field's description. Two new fields, **Session Client Session ID** and **Subsession Client Session ID**, put a session's and its subsession's IDs on the same row.

where.path: Reports → Report Builder → Fields

entries.use_case: Organizers can find a session field in a report under the name they already know from the Sessions grid. Teams that sync sessions with another system can show the session's and the subsession's own IDs side by side in one report.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer can't find a session field in the Report Builder ("where is Client Session ID?"), or needs a session + subsession report with their own system's IDs.
internal.who_should_get_it: Any customer building session reports, especially those syncing sessions with a registration or event app by Client Session ID.
internal.staff_path: Same as the customer.
internal.gotchas: Saved reports keep the column headers they were saved with; only columns added afterwards take the new names. On a subsession row, plain Client Session ID is the subsession's own value, which is often empty — use Session Client Session ID for the parent's.
internal.talk_track: The Report Builder now calls session fields what the Sessions grid calls them, so search for "Client Session ID" and it's there. For subsession reports, add Session Client Session ID to get the parent session's ID on every subsession row.

entries.title: Create campaign on an exhibitor or sponsor portal opens Quick Launch on Groups
entries.summary: On an exhibitor, sponsor or accounts portal, **Assign Items → Advocacy campaigns → Create campaign** now opens Quick Launch on the **Groups** audience with that portal already chosen under **By portal**. It used to open on **Speakers**, and the portal was missing from the list.

where.path: Portals → an exhibitor or sponsor portal → Assign Items → Advocacy campaigns → Create campaign

entries.use_case: Starting a sponsor or exhibitor share campaign from their portal now lands on the right audience with the portal already picked, so the campaign reaches that portal's companies without switching anything in Quick Launch.

cs_action.note: No existing campaign was created with the wrong audience (0 in US, EU and ME on 2026-10-29), so there is nothing to fix in customer data.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer says Create campaign on an exhibitor or sponsor portal put them on Speakers, or their portal was missing under By portal.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers with Exhibitor Pro or Sponsor Pro who run Advocacy for exhibitors or sponsors.
internal.staff_path: Portals → an Accounts-module portal → Assign Items → Advocacy campaigns → Create campaign
internal.gotchas: By portal needs Exhibitor Pro or Sponsor Pro. The link carries audience=groups&portalId=<portal>; a Contacts portal still opens on Speakers.
internal.talk_track: Create campaign on your exhibitor or sponsor portal now opens Quick Launch on Groups with that portal already selected, so the campaign goes straight to those companies.

entries.title: The description on a new portal file is saved
entries.summary: The **Description** you type in **Portals → Portal files → Add File** is now saved with the file, for uploads and for external URLs. It used to be dropped, so it only stuck if you edited the file afterwards.

where.path: Program → Portals → Portal files → Add → Add File → Description

entries.use_case: The line of context you add to a file ("Read before you arrive", "Updated 3 March") now shows on the portal the first time, without having to edit the file again.

cs_action.note: Files added before this release still have no description if one was typed at creation; the customer can add it with Edit on the file.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer says the description they typed on a portal file disappeared.
internal.who_should_get_it: Any customer sharing files through portals.
internal.staff_path: Program → Portals → Portal files → Add → Add File
internal.gotchas: The create endpoint still ignores description; the UI saves it with a follow-up update, the same call the edit panel uses. A file created through the API needs a separate update to set it.
internal.talk_track: The description you type when you add a portal file now sticks, so it shows under the title on the portal straight away.

entries.title: Create portal items, or describe them, from the Assign Items step
entries.summary: On a portal's **Assign Items** step, a **Create** menu, a **New** button on each section and a **Create "…"** row in **Add existing** create a task, form, file request, resource page, file or Advocacy campaign in place: one save puts it in the library and on this portal, with **Required** and due dates set there. **Describe it** drafts several items from one sentence for you to tick and add.

enable.path: Not customer-enabled yet: Sessionboard staff only

where.path: Portals → a portal → Assign Items → Create, a section's New button, or Describe it

entries.use_case: Building a portal no longer means a trip to each library and back: create the task, form, file request, page, file or campaign where you assign it, with its due date and Required set in the same place.

cs_action.note: Super users only (useSuperUser) while we QA it; there is no per-customer switch yet. Demo it, but don't promise a date.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer building portals complains about switching between the library and the portal editor.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers who build or rebuild speaker, exhibitor or sponsor portals every event.
internal.staff_path: Portals → a portal → Assign Items → Create (signed in as a super user)
internal.gotchas: Undo deletes the library item as well as the portal assignment; on a campaign it pauses instead, since a launched campaign may have sent. If assigning fails after the create, the item stays in the library and the toast offers Retry. File request presets fill the title and instructions only. Form templates need permission to manage fields; a question that cannot be created is skipped and named in a banner. Describe it needs web-api #4921 in production and never proposes files.
internal.talk_track: You can now create anything a portal holds right where you assign it, and Describe it drafts a first set of items from one sentence for you to review.

entries.title: Registration Reports: 46 ready-made reports and the report builder
entries.summary: A new **Reports** page under **Registration** gives organizers 46 ready-made reports — registrations by status, ticket and form, revenue, payments, refunds, credits, invoices, workshop rosters, check-in, session attendance, badge prints, promo codes, waitlists, approvals, cancellations, transfers, SMS delivery, seating, answers and more — in a searchable catalog. Open any report to run it in a dialog (50 rows per page) and download it as **CSV** or **Excel**. **Build a report** or **Customize, save or schedule** opens the full report builder pre-seeded with the report's query, to add columns, filters, grouping and sorting, save it to the **Saved reports** list, share a link or schedule email delivery. Reports respect **View registrations and orders** and **View finance reports**: a report the viewer cannot run is shown locked with the permission named.

where.path: Registration → Reports

entries.use_case: Organizers can answer revenue, attendance and logistics questions — how much money came in today, which workshops are full, who hasn't checked in — without exporting raw data or building queries from scratch. Finance staff get their own permission-gated view of payment and invoice reports without exposing that data to the rest of the team. Anyone can save or schedule a customised version for recurring use.

cs_action.note: Available on events with the Registration feature once both the API (web-api #4882) and the Reports page (web-ui-v2 #1284) are deployed; both are in shipped.prs. Finance reports are gated by the View finance reports permission — confirm the customer's finance team has that role before demoing revenue reports.

internal.when_to_bring_up: Any Registration customer asking how to pull revenue summaries, workshop rosters, check-in numbers or transfer history without a data export.
internal.who_should_get_it: Events using Registration (beta). Finance-sensitive reports require the View finance reports permission to be assigned.
internal.staff_path: Registration → Reports
internal.gotchas: The Registration category and all 46 recipes are hidden on events without the Registration feature flag. Finance fields (revenue, payments, invoices, credits, refunds) are refused at compile time for users without the finance permission — they get a 403, not empty data. Anonymised registrants show status, ticket and amounts but personal columns read 'Anonymised'. Voided registrations and orders are excluded unless the query explicitly includes deleted records. Downloads larger than the report's row limit are refused with a 422 error. In the Reports page, reports the viewer lacks permission to run are shown locked with the required permission named. The ?sbql= workbench seed only applies when no queryId is present.
internal.talk_track: You already have the report builder for sessions and speakers — Registration Reports brings that same experience to your attendee and revenue data, with 46 pre-built reports ready to run on day one.

draft.docs_gap: The linked guide /registration/reports exists in the article index but should document: how to navigate the Reports section, the full list of 46 ready-made report categories, how to use the report builder for registration data, permission requirements for finance reports, and how to schedule or export reports.
draft.why_use_it: Registration Reports brings the full Sessionboard report builder to your registration data, so you can slice registrations, orders, payments, workshops, check-ins and more the same way you already work with session and speaker data. Pick from 46 ready-made reports for the most common questions, or build your own with custom columns, filters, grouping and sorting. Save reports for your team, schedule them by email, and export to CSV or XLSX — all from one place inside Registration.

entries.title: Registration checkout, waitlist, refunds and onsite desk are more reliable under concurrent load
entries.summary: A set of concurrency and correctness fixes across registration checkout, waitlist autopay, refunds, workshop changes, walk-up card pricing, expo allotments and the onsite desk. Key changes registrants and organizers will notice: a checkout that races another for the last seat in a shared capacity pool now receives a clear **409 – seat unavailable** instead of an oversell; a price-tier change that happens while a cart is open returns **409 – price changed** with the old and new totals; a waitlist offer that has expired or whose hold has lapsed returns **409 – offer expired**; autopay only runs against cards (other payment methods are skipped with a **card only** notice); a walk-up card payment that no longer matches the quoted price is refused before any charge is attempted; an expo badge allotment whose hold expired is re-checked before payment; and anonymised registrants are blocked at the staffed desk, door, badge print and sync.

where.path: Registration → Orders; Registration → Waitlist; Onsite → Desk; Onsite → Badges

entries.use_case: Events with high-demand ticket releases or shared capacity pools no longer risk overselling seats when multiple registrants check out simultaneously. Organizers running waitlists with autopay get accurate decline messaging and are protected from double-charges on expired offers.

cs_action.note: Several new 409 error codes are now surfaced to registrants (price_changed, offer_expired, autopay_card_only, extra_badges_expired, change_in_progress, windows_mode_not_importable). Confirm that any custom registration confirmation flows or third-party integrations handle 409 responses gracefully before a high-traffic launch.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer reports oversells on shared-capacity tickets, double-charges on waitlist autopay, or asks why anonymised registrants were appearing at the onsite desk.
internal.who_should_get_it: Any customer using Registration with shared capacity pools, waitlist autopay, walk-up card payments, expo badge allotments, or the onsite staffed desk.
internal.staff_path: Registration → Orders; Registration → Waitlist; Onsite → Desk
internal.gotchas: Autopay now skips non-card payment methods entirely (logged as card_only) rather than attempting them. Payment-plan orders are excluded from autopay. entries.title: Public API contact, exhibitor and sponsor writes now advance `updated_at` correctly
entries.summary: Writes to contacts, exhibitors and sponsors via the public API (`PUT /contacts/{id}`, bulk contact updates, exhibitor and sponsor PUT/bulk) now advance `updated_at` on the underlying record after each write. Contact `GET`, list and write responses return the record's own `updated_at` — the same column the concurrency check compares — so echoing it back on a subsequent `PUT` returns **200** instead of **409 STALE_UPDATE**. Delta syncs that poll on `updated_at` will now pick up records changed through the API.

where.path: Public API — PUT /contacts/{id}, POST /contacts/bulk, PUT /exhibitors/{id}, PUT /sponsors/{id} and their bulk equivalents

entries.use_case: API integrations that write contacts, exhibitors or sponsors and then poll for changes — or that echo `updated_at` as a concurrency token — will now see accurate timestamps and stop receiving spurious 409 errors. Delta syncs will pick up records edited through the API on the next ETL run without requiring a manual admin touch.

cs_action.note: Any API integration that delta-syncs on contact updated_at, or that echoes updated_at as a concurrency token on PUT, was broken since PR #4806 went live (2026-10-29 03:00 UTC). Those integrations will now start seeing contacts as changed on the next poll. Flag partners with write:contacts tokens — US: 64 orgs, EU: 9 orgs — so they are not surprised by a sudden wave of 'changed' records.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer reports 409 STALE_UPDATE on contact PUT, stale search results after API writes, or a delta sync that never picks up API-written contacts.
internal.who_should_get_it: Any org using the public API to write contacts, exhibitors or sponsors, especially those running delta syncs or two-way integrations.
internal.gotchas: Integrations that diff on updated_at will now see API-written contacts as changed — including their own writes. This is correct behaviour but may surprise partners who relied on the old (broken) no-op. The field type and format are unchanged; only the value moves. Also note: the concurrency token on contact PUT and bulk update was 409-ing every echoed token since #4806 (2026-10-29 03:00 UTC) — all contacts written since then had mismatched stamps.
internal.talk_track: A bug introduced in a recent release caused contact PUT to return 409 on every echoed updated_at token, and API-written contacts never re-indexed for search. Both are fixed: the timestamp now advances on every write, and echoing it back works correctly.

draft.docs_gap: The API tokens guide should add a section explaining how updated_at is used as a concurrency token on PUT and bulk-update endpoints, and how delta syncs should use it as a watermark.
draft.why_use_it: The public API lets you read and write contacts, exhibitors, sponsors and sessions from your own systems. Use it to push data from a registration platform, CRM or custom integration, and to pull changes back for downstream tools. The `updated_at` field on each record is the concurrency token for conflict detection and the watermark for delta syncs, so keeping it accurate is essential for reliable two-way integrations.

entries.title: Pending registration payments now reconcile automatically, with a "Needs review" escalation path
entries.summary: A background reconciler now checks Spreedly every 5 minutes for registration charges left **pending** or **processing** — ACH / payment-plan charges, 3-D Secure holds, and walk-up or onsite card payments — and settles or fails them automatically. A charge still unresolved past a cutoff measured from the charge attempt (24 hours for cards, 240 hours — 10 days — for ACH), one the gateway has no record of, or one reported at a different amount becomes **Needs review**: its held seats are released and autopay is paused on the related installment. In the **Order drawer → Payments**, every unsettled payment shows a status badge, and a needs-review payment shows the reason and what to check in the gateway. **Registration → Orders → Finance reports → Failed transactions** gains a **Status** column and a **Show** filter (**All / Declined / No answer yet / Needs review**).

where.path: Registration → Orders → Order drawer → Payments; Registration → Orders → Finance reports → Failed transactions

entries.use_case: Events using ACH payment plans, 3-D Secure, or walk-up card payments no longer need manual follow-up when a charge stalls: the system settles it automatically or flags it for review and releases the held seats so they go back on sale — preventing phantom holds from blocking inventory.

cs_action.note: The reconciler runs automatically; no enablement needed. However, customers using ACH or payment plans should be told that long-pending charges will now appear in Failed transactions as 'Needs review' after 240 hours / 10 days (ACH) or 24 hours (card) from the charge attempt; until then the pending charge keeps its seats. Staff must review those rows and decide — nothing is auto-refunded or auto-voided. A payment settled after 'Needs review' can oversell by one seat because holds were already released. Both halves (web-api #4912 reconciler, web-ui-v2 #1296 badge and filter) are in shipped.prs.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer reports that a registration payment is stuck pending, seats are held but not confirmed, or they ask why an ACH or payment-plan charge never settled.
internal.who_should_get_it: Any customer using Registration with ACH, payment plans, 3-D Secure, walk-up card, or onsite card payments.
internal.staff_path: Registration → Orders → Finance reports → Failed transactions (Status: Needs review)
internal.gotchas: Needs-review rows are not polled again — a human must act. A charge that settles after escalation will confirm seats even though holds were released, which can oversell by one. Autopay is paused on the related installment when escalated; staff must manually resume or void. The reconciler uses SKIP LOCKED so concurrent runs are safe, but a charge in its first 2 minutes is not claimed. The order drawer names the reason (not confirmed in time, no gateway record, amount mismatch); the orders guide's Payments that need review section says what to do for each.
internal.talk_track: Pending charges — ACH, payment plans, 3-D Secure, walk-up cards — now settle automatically. If one can't resolve within the cutoff, it shows up in Failed transactions as 'Needs review' with a reason, and the held seats go back on sale so you're not stuck waiting.

draft.docs_gap: The guide should add a section on the new "Needs review" payment status: what triggers it, what happens to held seats and autopay installments, where to find these charges in Failed transactions, and what actions staff should take to resolve them.
draft.why_use_it: Registration payments that go through ACH, payment plans, 3-D Secure, or onsite card readers can take time to settle at the gateway. The reconciler handles that wait automatically: it checks each pending charge, confirms the result with Spreedly, and either completes the order — sending confirmation emails and converting holds to confirmed seats — or escalates it so you can act. Charges that cannot be resolved within the cutoff window appear in Failed transactions with a reason, and their seats are released so you can resell them without manual intervention.
